ownershipHistory.summary: Azik demonstrates the old copper whistle and throws it to Klein so Klein can summon Azik's messenger when he needs to send a letter.
After resurrecting and visiting his own grave, Klein recovers the copper whistle that had been buried with him.
After escaping Amon, Klein notes that he had safely placed Azik's copper whistle above the gray fog before losing several other items.
During the Roselle exhibition operation, Klein takes the suspicious bookmark together with decoys and transfers the bookmarks above the gray fog for safekeeping.
Klein discovers the bookmark's opening incantation and activates it as the Black Emperor Card of Blasphemy, revealing the pathway information within.
Klein deliberately keeps the Black Emperor Card above the gray fog as a precaution after confirming its nature.
Creeping Hunger is introduced as Vice Admiral Hurricane Qilangos's dangerous mystical glove before Klein ever owns it.
Klein receives Azik's letter confirming that Azik obtained Creeping Hunger after killing Qilangos.
Azik hands the sealed glove to Klein after recovering the memories he needed from it; Klein becomes its active holder.
After Klein's escape from Amon and eventual suicide, he explicitly lists Creeping Hunger among the valuable items he lost and mourns its loss.
After Kalvetua's death, Klein retrieves the white scepter and names the Sealed Artifact Sea God Scepter before taking it above the gray fog.
Klein tests the scepter and establishes its sea, storm, flight, prayer-response, and navigation powers together with its negative effects.
Before entering slumber, The Fool tells Alger that he can bring the Sea God Scepter for his coming mission while the Sea God prayers are redirected to Klein.
Ukfa introduces the mystical revolver called Death Knell and Klein shows immediate interest in purchasing it.
Klein receives, evaluates, and purchases Death Knell for 9,000 pounds while maintaining the Gehrman Sparrow persona.
Klein lists Death Knell among the valuable equipment lost after the Amon escape and his eventual suicide.
Klein first directly interacts with the living silver mirror and Arrodes unexpectedly calls itself his loyal and humble servant.
Arrodes independently reports to Klein through a reflective surface, reinforcing its unusual loyalty despite not belonging to him.
During the Merlin Hermes period, Klein leaves Constant carrying his suitcase with Arrodes accompanying him, reflecting their established companion relationship rather than conventional ownership.
